policy_title: Reform social housing law to prioritise local people
stated: Reform UK will reform social housing law to prioritise local people and those who have paid into the system, stating that foreign nationals must go to the back of the queue.

source.quote: Reform Social Housing Law Prioritise local people and those who have paid into the system. Foreign nationals must go to the back of the queue. Not the front.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly governs social housing allocation rules, determining which applicants can access social/affordable housing stock and on what priority basis — a core O1 indicator.

The policy explicitly mandates differential legal treatment of foreign nationals (including those potentially with settled status or refugee leave) in access to social housing, engaging equal-treatment and anti-discrimination law — a genuine O9 verdict on whether rights of a defined group are protected or curtailed.

Institutionalising a formal 'back of the queue' rule for foreign nationals in public housing allocation concretely affects sense of belonging, social trust, and inter-group relations for immigrant communities — all specific O15 indicators.

membership_note: The policy redistributes access to existing social housing stock but does not change supply, prices, or aggregate affordability indicators, so O1 does not earn a real verdict. The dominant effects are the equal-treatment question (O9) and the community-cohesion/belonging question (O15).
